WITH artifact_cpi AS
  (SELECT a.artdynasty AS dynasty,
          ((r.histsignrating + r.researchvalrating + r.cultscore) * (10 - CASE a.conservestatus
                                                                              WHEN 'Excellent' THEN 1
                                                                              WHEN 'Good' THEN 3
                                                                              WHEN 'Fair' THEN 5
                                                                              WHEN 'Poor' THEN 7
                                                                              WHEN 'Critical' THEN 10
                                                                          END)) / 30.0 AS cpi,
          CASE c.budgetallocstatus
              WHEN 'Adequate' THEN 1.0
              WHEN 'Review Required' THEN 0.5
              WHEN 'Insufficient' THEN 0.0
              ELSE 0.0
          END AS budget_ratio,
          CASE
              WHEN c.budgetallocstatus = 'Adequate' THEN 1
              ELSE 0
          END AS adequate_flag,
          CASE
              WHEN c.budgetallocstatus = 'Insufficient' THEN 1
              ELSE 0
          END AS insufficient_flag,
          CASE
              WHEN a.conservestatus = 'Critical'
                   AND c.budgetallocstatus = 'Insufficient' THEN 1
              ELSE 0
          END AS crisis_flag
   FROM artifactscore a
   JOIN artifactratings r ON r.artref = a.artregistry
   JOIN conservationandmaintenance c ON c.artrefmaintained = a.artregistry),
     dynasty_agg AS
  (SELECT dynasty,
          SUM(cpi) AS total_cpi,
          SUM(adequate_flag) AS adequate_funding_count,
          SUM(insufficient_flag) AS insufficient_funding_count,
          SUM(cpi * budget_ratio) AS cbe_num,
          COUNT(*) AS artifact_count,
          SUM(crisis_flag) AS critical_insufficient_count
   FROM artifact_cpi
   GROUP BY dynasty)
SELECT dynasty,
       total_conservation_priority_index,
       adequate_funding_count,
       insufficient_funding_count,
       cbe,
       budget_status
FROM
  (SELECT dynasty,
          total_cpi AS total_conservation_priority_index,
          adequate_funding_count,
          insufficient_funding_count,
          cbe_num / artifact_count AS cbe,
          CASE
              WHEN cbe_num / artifact_count < 0.5
                   AND critical_insufficient_count > 0 THEN 'Budget Crisis'
              ELSE 'Within Budget'
          END AS budget_status,
          0 AS sort_order
   FROM dynasty_agg
   UNION ALL SELECT 'ALL DYNASTIES',
                    SUM(total_cpi),
                    SUM(adequate_funding_count),
                    SUM(insufficient_funding_count),
                    SUM(cbe_num) / SUM(artifact_count),
                    CASE
                        WHEN SUM(cbe_num) / SUM(artifact_count) < 0.5
                             AND SUM(critical_insufficient_count) > 0 THEN 'Budget Crisis'
                        ELSE 'Within Budget'
                    END,
                    1
   FROM dynasty_agg) AS combined
ORDER BY sort_order,
         dynasty;

<domain_knowledge>
- Maintenance overdue: At least one immediate maintenance or testing action is required. Selects 95% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(maintstatus) = 'Overdue' OR filterstatus = 'Replace Now' OR TRIM(silicagelstatus) = 'Replace Now' OR inertgassysstatus = 'Maintenance' OR firesuppresssys = 'Maintenance' OR TRIM(empowerstatus) = 'Testing' OR backupsysstatus = 'Testing' OR sealcondition = 'Poor'
- Cleaning interval days (cleanintervaldays): Number of days between the last cleaning date and the next cleaning due date. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: cleanintervaldays = JULIANDAY(nextcleaningdue) - JULIANDAY(lastcleaningdate)
- Conservation difficulty: Level of effort needed to conserve an artifact, inferred from stability and deterioration. Selects 32% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid' THEN 'High' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Medium' END
- High conservation difficulty cohort: Artifacts requiring high conservation effort due to unstable material or rapid deterioration. Selects 17% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = 'High' AND (matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid')
- Stable artifact cohort: Artifacts with stable material, slow deterioration, and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- High public access artifact cohort: Artifacts suitable for high public access based on stability and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: publicaccessrating >= 8 AND matstability = 'Stable' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- Active security systems: Hall with full CCTV coverage and all security systems active or armed. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: cctvcoverage = 'Full' AND motiondetectstatus = 'Active' AND TRIM(alarmsysstatus) = 'Armed' AND accessctrlstatus = 'Active'
- Maintenance needed: Hall with at least one security subsystem under maintenance. Selects 72% of rows.
  Definition: motiondetectstatus = 'Maintenance' OR TRIM(alarmsysstatus) = 'Maintenance' OR accessctrlstatus = 'Maintenance'
- Deterioration rate: Rate at which an artifact deteriorates, inferred from material stability. Selects 35% of rows.
  Definition: deteriorrate = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' THEN 'Rapid' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' THEN 'Slow' ELSE 'Moderate' END
- Treatment complexity: Complexity of artifact treatment, inferred from conservation difficulty. Selects 34% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(treatcomplexity) = CASE WHEN conservediff = 'High' THEN 'Complex' WHEN conservediff = 'Low' THEN 'Simple' ELSE 'Moderate' END
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
I want to see which historical periods have adequate conservation resources and which might be facing a Conservation Budget Crisis. For each dynasty, show the dynasty name, their total conservation priority index, the count of artifacts with adequate funding, the count with insufficient funding, the calculated CBE valuea, and a budget status that indicates 'Budget Crisis' if the dynasty meets the defined Conservation Budget Crisis criteria, and 'Within Budget' otherwise. Besides, please include a summary row for all dynasties combined labeled as 'ALL DYNASTIES'.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Conservation Budget Efficiency (CBE): Measures the efficiency of conservation budget allocation relative to artifact importance.
  Definition: CBE = (SUM_i in artifacts (CPI_i * BudgetRatio_i)) / (COUNT(artifacts)), where BudgetRatio is the proportion of total conservation budget allocated to each artifact
- Conservation Budget Crisis: Identifies when conservation budget allocation is insufficient for high-priority artifacts.
  Definition: Occurs when CBE < 0.5 AND at least one artifact has ConserveStatus='Critical' and BudgetAllocStatus='Insufficient'.
- Conservation Priority Index (CPI): Calculates the overall conservation priority for an artifact based on multiple factors.
  Definition: CPI = ((HistSignRating + ResearchValRating + CultScore) * (10 - ConserveStatus)) / (30), where ConserveStatus is numerically mapped: Excellent=1, Good=3, Fair=5, Poor=7, Critical=10
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH artifact_cpi AS (
  SELECT
    a.artdynasty AS dynasty,
    ((r.histsignrating + r.researchvalrating + r.cultscore)
      * (10 - CASE a.conservestatus
          WHEN 'Excellent' THEN 1
          WHEN 'Good' THEN 3
          WHEN 'Fair' THEN 5
          WHEN 'Poor' THEN 7
          WHEN 'Critical' THEN 10
        END)
    ) / 30.0 AS cpi,
    CASE c.budgetallocstatus
      WHEN 'Adequate' THEN 1.0
      WHEN 'Review Required' THEN 0.5
      WHEN 'Insufficient' THEN 0.0
      ELSE 0.0
    END AS budget_ratio,
    CASE WHEN c.budgetallocstatus = 'Adequate' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS adequate_flag,
    CASE WHEN c.budgetallocstatus = 'Insufficient' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS insufficient_flag,
    CASE WHEN a.conservestatus = 'Critical' AND c.budgetallocstatus = 'Insufficient' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS crisis_flag
  FROM artifactscore a
  JOIN artifactratings r ON r.artref = a.artregistry
  JOIN conservationandmaintenance c ON c.artrefmaintained = a.artregistry
),
dynasty_agg AS (
  SELECT
    dynasty,
    SUM(cpi) AS total_cpi,
    SUM(adequate_flag) AS adequate_funding_count,
    SUM(insufficient_flag) AS insufficient_funding_count,
    SUM(cpi * budget_ratio) AS cbe_num,
    COUNT(*) AS artifact_count,
    SUM(crisis_flag) AS critical_insufficient_count
  FROM artifact_cpi
  GROUP BY dynasty
)
SELECT dynasty, total_conservation_priority_index, adequate_funding_count, insufficient_funding_count, cbe, budget_status
FROM (
  SELECT
    dynasty,
    total_cpi AS total_conservation_priority_index,
    adequate_funding_count,
    insufficient_funding_count,
    cbe_num / artifact_count AS cbe,
    CASE WHEN cbe_num / artifact_count < 0.5 AND critical_insufficient_count > 0 THEN 'Budget Crisis' ELSE 'Within Budget' END AS budget_status,
    0 AS sort_order
  FROM dynasty_agg
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'ALL DYNASTIES',
    SUM(total_cpi),
    SUM(adequate_funding_count),
    SUM(insufficient_funding_count),
    SUM(cbe_num) / SUM(artifact_count),
    CASE WHEN SUM(cbe_num) / SUM(artifact_count) < 0.5 AND SUM(critical_insufficient_count) > 0 THEN 'Budget Crisis' ELSE 'Within Budget' END,
    1
  FROM dynasty_agg
) AS combined
ORDER BY sort_order, dynasty;

                                                                     WHEN 'High' THEN 10
                                                                     WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5
                                                                     WHEN 'Low' THEN 1
                                                                     ELSE 0
                                                                 END + CASE TRIM(sd.storagesensitivity)
                                                                           WHEN 'High' THEN 10
                                                                           WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5
                                                                           WHEN 'Low' THEN 1
                                                                           ELSE 0
                                                                       END) AS total_weight,
          (CASE
               WHEN sd.envsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END + CASE
                     WHEN sd.lightsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                     ELSE 0
                 END + CASE
                           WHEN sd.tempsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                           ELSE 0
                       END + CASE
                                 WHEN sd.humiditysensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                                 ELSE 0
                             END + CASE
                                       WHEN sd.vibrasensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                                       ELSE 0
                                   END + CASE
                                             WHEN sd.pollutantsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                                             ELSE 0
                                         END + CASE
                                                   WHEN sd.pestsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                                                   ELSE 0
                                               END + CASE
                                                         WHEN sd.handlesensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                                                         ELSE 0
                                                     END + CASE
                                                               WHEN sd.transportsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                                                               ELSE 0
                                                           END + CASE
                                                                     WHEN sd.displaysensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                                                                     ELSE 0
                                                                 END + CASE
                                                                           WHEN sd.storagesensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1
                                                                           ELSE 0
                                                                       END) AS sensitivity_count,
          (CASE
               WHEN TRIM(sd.envsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END + CASE
                     WHEN TRIM(sd.lightsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                     ELSE 0
                 END + CASE
                           WHEN TRIM(sd.tempsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                           ELSE 0
                       END + CASE
                                 WHEN TRIM(sd.humiditysensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                                 ELSE 0
                             END + CASE
                                       WHEN TRIM(sd.vibrasensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                                       ELSE 0
                                   END + CASE
                                             WHEN TRIM(sd.pollutantsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                                             ELSE 0
                                         END + CASE
                                                   WHEN TRIM(sd.pestsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                                                   ELSE 0
                                               END + CASE
                                                         WHEN TRIM(sd.handlesensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                                                         ELSE 0
                                                     END + CASE
                                                               WHEN TRIM(sd.transportsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                                                               ELSE 0
                                                           END + CASE
                                                                     WHEN TRIM(sd.displaysensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                                                                     ELSE 0
                                                                 END + CASE
                                                                           WHEN TRIM(sd.storagesensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1
                                                                           ELSE 0
                                                                       END) AS high_sensitivity_count
   FROM sensitivitydata sd)
SELECT a.artregistry,
       a.artname,
       e.tempc,
       e.relhumidity,
       COALESCE(sm.high_sensitivity_count, 0) AS high_sensitivity_count,
       CASE
           WHEN (a.artageyears * (CAST(sm.total_weight AS REAL) / NULLIF(sm.sensitivity_count, 0)) * (e.relhumidity - 50) * (e.relhumidity - 50) * e.tempc / 100000.0) > 5
                AND COALESCE(sm.high_sensitivity_count, 0) >= 2 THEN 'Yes'
           ELSE 'No'
       END AS meets_accelerated_deterioration_criteria
FROM artifactscore a
LEFT JOIN usagerecords u ON TRIM(u.artrefused) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
LEFT JOIN environmentalreadingscore e ON TRIM(e.showcaseref) = TRIM(u.showcaserefused)
LEFT JOIN sensitivity_metrics sm ON TRIM(sm.artref) = TRIM(a.artregistry);

- Conservation difficulty: Level of effort needed to conserve an artifact, inferred from stability and deterioration. Selects 32% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid' THEN 'High' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Medium' END
- High conservation difficulty cohort: Artifacts requiring high conservation effort due to unstable material or rapid deterioration. Selects 17% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = 'High' AND (matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid')
- Stable artifact cohort: Artifacts with stable material, slow deterioration, and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- High public access artifact cohort: Artifacts suitable for high public access based on stability and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: publicaccessrating >= 8 AND matstability = 'Stable' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- 24-hour temperature variation (tempvar24h): Difference between maximum and minimum temperature recorded by a monitor in the preceding 24 hours.
  Definition: tempvar24h = MAX(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) - MIN(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
- 24-hour humidity variation (humvar24h): Difference between maximum and minimum relative humidity recorded by a monitor in the preceding 24 hours.
  Definition: humvar24h = MAX(relhumidity) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) - MIN(relhumidity) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)

<task>
Show me whether items are in Accelerated Deterioration, along with artifact's ID and name, the current temperature and humidity in their display case, how many high sensitivities they have, and whether they meet the accelerated deterioration criteria ('Yes' or 'No').
<definitions> MUST USE
- Material Deterioration Rate (MDR): Estimates the rate of material deterioration based on environmental factors.
  Definition: MDR = (ArtAgeYears * ERF * (RelHumidity - 50)^2 * TempC) / (100000), where higher values indicate faster deterioration
- Accelerated Deterioration Scenario: Identifies conditions that could lead to rapid artifact deterioration.
  Definition: Occurs when MDR > 5 AND at least two SensitivityData values are 'High'.
- Environmental Risk Factor (ERF): Quantifies the overall environmental risk to an artifact based on its sensitivities.
  Definition: ERF = (SUM_i in sensitivities SensWeight_i) / (COUNT(sensitivities)), where sensitivities includes EnvSensitivity, LightSensitivity, TempSensitivity, etc, with value mapping based on Sensitivity Weight Values.
- Sensitivity Weight Values: Numerical weights for sensitivity calculations
  Definition: EnvSensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10; LightSensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10; TempSensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10; HumiditySensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

```sql
WITH sensitivity_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        sd.artref,
        (
            CASE TRIM(sd.envsensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.lightsensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.tempsensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.humiditysensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.vibrasensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.pollutantsensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.pestsensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.handlesensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.transportsensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.displaysensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE TRIM(sd.storagesensitivity) WHEN 'High' THEN 10 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        ) AS total_weight,
        (
            CASE WHEN sd.envsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.lightsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.tempsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.humiditysensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.vibrasensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.pollutantsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.pestsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.handlesensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.transportsensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.displaysensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN sd.storagesensitivity IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        ) AS sensitivity_count,
        (
            CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.envsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.lightsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.tempsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.humiditysensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.vibrasensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.pollutantsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.pestsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.handlesensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.transportsensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.displaysensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
            + CASE WHEN TRIM(sd.storagesensitivity) = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
        ) AS high_sensitivity_count
    FROM sensitivitydata sd
)
SELECT
    a.artregistry,
    a.artname,
    e.tempc,
    e.relhumidity,
    COALESCE(sm.high_sensitivity_count, 0) AS high_sensitivity_count,
    CASE WHEN
        (
            a.artageyears
            * (CAST(sm.total_weight AS REAL) / NULLIF(sm.sensitivity_count, 0))
            * (e.relhumidity - 50)
            * (e.relhumidity - 50)
            * e.tempc
            / 100000.0
        ) > 5
        AND COALESCE(sm.high_sensitivity_count, 0) >= 2
        THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No'
    END AS meets_accelerated_deterioration_criteria
FROM artifactscore a
LEFT JOIN usagerecords u ON TRIM(u.artrefused) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
LEFT JOIN environmentalreadingscore e ON TRIM(e.showcaseref) = TRIM(u.showcaserefused)
LEFT JOIN sensitivity_metrics sm ON TRIM(sm.artref) = TRIM(a.artregistry);
```

- 24-hour temperature variation (tempvar24h): Difference between maximum and minimum temperature recorded by a monitor in the preceding 24 hours.
  Definition: tempvar24h = MAX(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) - MIN(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
- 24-hour humidity variation (humvar24h): Difference between maximum and minimum relative humidity recorded by a monitor in the preceding 24 hours.
  Definition: humvar24h = MAX(relhumidity) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) - MIN(relhumidity) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
- Cleaning interval days (cleanintervaldays): Number of days between the last cleaning date and the next cleaning due date. Selects 1% of rows.

- Conservation difficulty: Level of effort needed to conserve an artifact, inferred from stability and deterioration. Selects 32% of rows.

- Maintenance overdue: At least one immediate maintenance or testing action is required. Selects 95% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(maintstatus) = 'Overdue' OR filterstatus = 'Replace Now' OR TRIM(silicagelstatus) = 'Replace Now' OR inertgassysstatus = 'Maintenance' OR firesuppresssys = 'Maintenance' OR TRIM(empowerstatus) = 'Testing' OR backupsysstatus = 'Testing' OR sealcondition = 'Poor'
- Conservation difficulty: Level of effort needed to conserve an artifact, inferred from stability and deterioration. Selects 32% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid' THEN 'High' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Medium' END
- High conservation difficulty cohort: Artifacts requiring high conservation effort due to unstable material or rapid deterioration. Selects 17% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = 'High' AND (matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid')
- Stable artifact cohort: Artifacts with stable material, slow deterioration, and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- High public access artifact cohort: Artifacts suitable for high public access based on stability and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: publicaccessrating >= 8 AND matstability = 'Stable' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- 24-hour temperature variation (tempvar24h): Difference between maximum and minimum temperature recorded by a monitor in the preceding 24 hours.
  Definition: tempvar24h = MAX(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) - MIN(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
- Active security systems: Hall with full CCTV coverage and all security systems active or armed. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: cctvcoverage = 'Full' AND motiondetectstatus = 'Active' AND TRIM(alarmsysstatus) = 'Armed' AND accessctrlstatus = 'Active'
- Maintenance needed: Hall with at least one security subsystem under maintenance. Selects 72% of rows.
  Definition: motiondetectstatus = 'Maintenance' OR TRIM(alarmsysstatus) = 'Maintenance' OR accessctrlstatus = 'Maintenance'
- Cleaning interval days (cleanintervaldays): Number of days between the last cleaning date and the next cleaning due date. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: cleanintervaldays = JULIANDAY(nextcleaningdue) - JULIANDAY(lastcleaningdate)

- Showcase Environmental Stability Rating (SESR): Measures how well a showcase maintains stable environmental conditions.
  Definition: SESR = 10 - ((TempVar24h + (HumVar24h) / (5) + LeakRate)) / (3), where higher scores indicate more stable showcases

FROM showcases AS s
JOIN environmentalreadingscore AS e

instances.question:
Identify all artifacts with high or medium light sensitivity. For each artifact, provide its registry number, name, material type, light sensitivity, and current exposure status ('Over Exposure' if maximum sensitivity in lux is above Light Exposure Thresholds, and 'Within Limits' otherwise).
<definitions> MUST USE
- SensitivityData.LightSensitivity: Illustrates light sensitivity classifications and their implications.
  Definition: Values include 'Low' (can tolerate up to 300 lux, like stone artifacts), 'Medium' (should be limited to 150-200 lux, like oil paintings), and 'High' (restricted to 50 lux or less, like textiles and works on paper).
</definitions>

candidates:
SELECT a.artregistry,
       a.artname,
       a.mattype,
       s.lightsensitivity,
       CASE
           WHEN MAX(l.lightlux) > CASE TRIM(s.lightsensitivity)
                                      WHEN 'High' THEN 50
                                      WHEN 'Medium' THEN 200
                                  END THEN 'Over Exposure'
           ELSE 'Within Limits'
       END AS current_exposure_status
FROM artifactscore a
JOIN sensitivitydata s ON TRIM(s.artref) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
LEFT JOIN conditionassessments c ON TRIM(c.artrefexamined) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
LEFT JOIN lightandradiationreadings l ON l.lightradregistry = c.lightreadrefobserved
WHERE TRIM(s.lightsensitivity) IN ('High',
                                   'Medium')
GROUP BY a.artregistry,
         a.artname,
         a.mattype,
         s.lightsensitivity
ORDER BY a.artregistry;

       a.mattype,
       s.lightsensitivity,
       CASE
           WHEN MAX(l.lightlux) > m.threshold THEN 'Over Exposure'
           ELSE 'Within Limits'
       END AS current_exposure_status
FROM artifactscore a
JOIN sensitivitydata s ON TRIM(s.artref) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
JOIN
  (SELECT 'High' AS sensitivity,
          50 AS threshold
   UNION ALL SELECT 'Medium',
                    200) m ON TRIM(s.lightsensitivity) = m.sensitivity
LEFT JOIN conditionassessments c ON TRIM(c.artrefexamined) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
LEFT JOIN lightandradiationreadings l ON l.lightradregistry = c.lightreadrefobserved
WHERE TRIM(s.lightsensitivity) IN ('High',
                                   'Medium')
GROUP BY a.artregistry,
         a.artname,
         a.mattype,
         s.lightsensitivity,
         m.threshold
ORDER BY a.artregistry;

- Conservation difficulty: Level of effort needed to conserve an artifact, inferred from stability and deterioration. Selects 32% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid' THEN 'High' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Medium' END
- High conservation difficulty cohort: Artifacts requiring high conservation effort due to unstable material or rapid deterioration. Selects 17% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = 'High' AND (matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid')
- Stable artifact cohort: Artifacts with stable material, slow deterioration, and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- High public access artifact cohort: Artifacts suitable for high public access based on stability and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: publicaccessrating >= 8 AND matstability = 'Stable' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- Maintenance overdue: At least one immediate maintenance or testing action is required. Selects 95% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(maintstatus) = 'Overdue' OR filterstatus = 'Replace Now' OR TRIM(silicagelstatus) = 'Replace Now' OR inertgassysstatus = 'Maintenance' OR firesuppresssys = 'Maintenance' OR TRIM(empowerstatus) = 'Testing' OR backupsysstatus = 'Testing' OR sealcondition = 'Poor'
- Deterioration rate: Rate at which an artifact deteriorates, inferred from material stability. Selects 35% of rows.

<task>
Identify all artifacts with high or medium light sensitivity. For each artifact, provide its registry number, name, material type, light sensitivity, and current exposure status ('Over Exposure' if maximum sensitivity in lux is above Light Exposure Thresholds, and 'Within Limits' otherwise).
<definitions> MUST USE
- SensitivityData.LightSensitivity: Illustrates light sensitivity classifications and their implications.
  Definition: Values include 'Low' (can tolerate up to 300 lux, like stone artifacts), 'Medium' (should be limited to 150-200 lux, like oil paintings), and 'High' (restricted to 50 lux or less, like textiles and works on paper).
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

SELECT
    a.artregistry,
    a.artname,
    a.mattype,
    s.lightsensitivity,
    CASE
        WHEN MAX(l.lightlux) > CASE TRIM(s.lightsensitivity)
                                   WHEN 'High' THEN 50
                                   WHEN 'Medium' THEN 200
                              END
        THEN 'Over Exposure'
        ELSE 'Within Limits'
    END AS current_exposure_status
FROM artifactscore a
JOIN sensitivitydata s ON TRIM(s.artref) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
LEFT JOIN conditionassessments c ON TRIM(c.artrefexamined) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
LEFT JOIN lightandradiationreadings l ON l.lightradregistry = c.lightreadrefobserved
WHERE TRIM(s.lightsensitivity) IN ('High', 'Medium')
GROUP BY a.artregistry, a.artname, a.mattype, s.lightsensitivity
ORDER BY a.artregistry;

instances.question:
Flag the top 10 collection pieces in greatest danger using the museum's Total Environmental Threat Level formula. Just give me their IDs and TETL scores - I need to see which need urgent protection first.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Total Environmental Threat Level (TETL): Comprehensive measurement of all environmental threats to an artifact based on multiple risk factors.
  Definition: TETL = ERF + LER + (MDR * 2), where ERF is the Environmental Risk Factor, LER is the Light Exposure Risk, and MDR is the Material Deterioration Rat.
- Environmental Risk Factor (ERF): Quantifies the overall environmental risk to an artifact based on its sensitivities.
  Definition: ERF = (SUM_i in sensitivities SensWeight_i) / (COUNT(sensitivities)), where sensitivities includes EnvSensitivity, LightSensitivity, TempSensitivity, etc, with value mapping based on Sensitivity Weight Values.
- Light Exposure Risk (LER): Quantifies the risk from light exposure based on artifact sensitivity and current light levels.
  Definition: LER = (LightLux * LightSensWeight * VisibleExpLxh) / (1000), where LightSensWeight uses Sensitivity Weight Values
- Material Deterioration Rate (MDR): Estimates the rate of material deterioration based on environmental factors.
  Definition: MDR = (ArtAgeYears * ERF * (RelHumidity - 50)^2 * TempC) / (100000), where higher values indicate faster deterioration
- Sensitivity Weight Values: Numerical weights for sensitivity calculations
  Definition: EnvSensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10; LightSensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10; TempSensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10; HumiditySensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10
</definitions>

<domain_knowledge>
- Conservation difficulty: Level of effort needed to conserve an artifact, inferred from stability and deterioration. Selects 32% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid' THEN 'High' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Medium' END
- High conservation difficulty cohort: Artifacts requiring high conservation effort due to unstable material or rapid deterioration. Selects 17% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = 'High' AND (matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid')
- Stable artifact cohort: Artifacts with stable material, slow deterioration, and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- High public access artifact cohort: Artifacts suitable for high public access based on stability and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: publicaccessrating >= 8 AND matstability = 'Stable' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- 24-hour temperature variation (tempvar24h): Difference between maximum and minimum temperature recorded by a monitor in the preceding 24 hours.
  Definition: tempvar24h = MAX(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) - MIN(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
- 24-hour humidity variation (humvar24h): Difference between maximum and minimum relative humidity recorded by a monitor in the preceding 24 hours.
  Definition: humvar24h = MAX(relhumidity) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) - MIN(relhumidity) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
- Treatment complexity: Complexity of artifact treatment, inferred from conservation difficulty. Selects 34% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(treatcomplexity) = CASE WHEN conservediff = 'High' THEN 'Complex' WHEN conservediff = 'Low' THEN 'Simple' ELSE 'Moderate' END
- visitorflowrate: Visitor flow rate category derived from daily visitor count thresholds. Selects 36% of rows.
  Definition: visitorflowrate = CASE WHEN visitorcountdaily < 400 THEN 'Low' WHEN visitorcountdaily < 800 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'High' END

- Total Environmental Threat Level (TETL): Comprehensive measurement of all environmental threats to an artifact based on multiple risk factors.
  Definition: TETL = ERF + LER + (MDR * 2), where ERF is the Environmental Risk Factor, LER is the Light Exposure Risk, and MDR is the Material Deterioration Rat.
- Environmental Risk Factor (ERF): Quantifies the overall environmental risk to an artifact based on its sensitivities.
  Definition: ERF = (SUM_i in sensitivities SensWeight_i) / (COUNT(sensitivities)), where sensitivities includes EnvSensitivity, LightSensitivity, TempSensitivity, etc, with value mapping based on Sensitivity Weight Values.
- Light Exposure Risk (LER): Quantifies the risk from light exposure based on artifact sensitivity and current light levels.

- Material Deterioration Rate (MDR): Estimates the rate of material deterioration based on environmental factors.
  Definition: MDR = (ArtAgeYears * ERF * (RelHumidity - 50)^2 * TempC) / (100000), where higher values indicate faster deterioration
- Sensitivity Weight Values: Numerical weights for sensitivity calculations
  Definition: EnvSensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10; LightSensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10; TempSensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10; HumiditySensitivity: Low=1, Medium=5, High=10

WITH risk AS (
  SELECT
    TRIM(a.artregistry) AS id,
    a.artageyears,
    er.tempc,
    er.relhumidity,
    lr.lightlux,
    lr.visibleexplxh,
    (
      (CASE TRIM(s.envsensitivity) WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'High' THEN 10 END)
      + (CASE TRIM(s.lightsensitivity) WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'High' THEN 10 END)
      + (CASE TRIM(s.tempsensitivity) WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'High' THEN 10 END)
      + (CASE TRIM(s.humiditysensitivity) WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'High' THEN 10 END)
    ) / 4.0 AS erf,
    CASE TRIM(s.lightsensitivity) WHEN 'Low' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 5 WHEN 'High' THEN 10 END AS light_weight
  FROM artifactscore a
  JOIN sensitivitydata s ON TRIM(s.artref) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
  JOIN conditionassessments ca ON TRIM(ca.artrefexamined) = TRIM(a.artregistry)
  JOIN lightandradiationreadings lr ON lr.lightradregistry = ca.lightreadrefobserved
  JOIN environmentalreadingscore er ON er.envreadregistry = lr.envreadref
)
SELECT
  id,
  erf
  + (lightlux * light_weight * visibleexplxh) / 1000.0
  + ((artageyears * erf * (relhumidity - 50) * (relhumidity - 50) * tempc) / 100000.0) * 2 AS tetl
FROM risk
ORDER BY tetl DESC
LIMIT 10;

- Maintenance overdue: At least one immediate maintenance or testing action is required. Selects 95% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(maintstatus) = 'Overdue' OR filterstatus = 'Replace Now' OR TRIM(silicagelstatus) = 'Replace Now' OR inertgassysstatus = 'Maintenance' OR firesuppresssys = 'Maintenance' OR TRIM(empowerstatus) = 'Testing' OR backupsysstatus = 'Testing' OR sealcondition = 'Poor'
- Conservation difficulty: Level of effort needed to conserve an artifact, inferred from stability and deterioration. Selects 32% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid' THEN 'High' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Medium' END
- High conservation difficulty cohort: Artifacts requiring high conservation effort due to unstable material or rapid deterioration. Selects 17% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = 'High' AND (matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid')
- Stable artifact cohort: Artifacts with stable material, slow deterioration, and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- High public access artifact cohort: Artifacts suitable for high public access based on stability and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: publicaccessrating >= 8 AND matstability = 'Stable' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- Fully compliant record: Usage record with current certification, Compliant compliance status, Passed audit, and Passed quality control. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: certstatus = 'Current' AND compliancestatus = 'Compliant' AND auditstatus = 'Passed' AND qualityctrlstatus = 'Passed'
- At-risk record: Usage record with expired certification, Non-compliant compliance status, Failed audit, or Failed quality control. Selects 82% of rows.
  Definition: certstatus = 'Expired' OR compliancestatus = 'Non-compliant' OR auditstatus = 'Failed' OR qualityctrlstatus = 'Failed'
- Cleaning interval days (cleanintervaldays): Number of days between the last cleaning date and the next cleaning due date. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: cleanintervaldays = JULIANDAY(nextcleaningdue) - JULIANDAY(lastcleaningdate)
- Deterioration rate: Rate at which an artifact deteriorates, inferred from material stability. Selects 35% of rows.
  Definition: deteriorrate = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' THEN 'Rapid' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' THEN 'Slow' ELSE 'Moderate' END
- Treatment complexity: Complexity of artifact treatment, inferred from conservation difficulty. Selects 34% of rows.

The view should show the CPI calculation with example parameters: historical significance of 5, research value of 7, cultural score of 8, and conservation status of 'Excellent'. Include the input parameters and the calculated CPI result, using appropriate type casting to REAL for accurate decimal computation and applying the standard conservation status mapping (Excellent=1, Good=3, Fair=5, Poor=7, Critical=10, default=5).

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS calculate_cpi_demo AS

<domain_knowledge>
- total gaseous pollutants (TGP): Sum of measured gaseous pollutant concentrations in parts per billion
  Definition: tvocppb + ozoneppb + so2ppb + no2ppb
- 24-hour temperature variation (tempvar24h): Difference between maximum and minimum temperature recorded by a monitor in the preceding 24 hours.
  Definition: tempvar24h = MAX(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) - MIN(tempc) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
- 24-hour humidity variation (humvar24h): Difference between maximum and minimum relative humidity recorded by a monitor in the preceding 24 hours.
  Definition: humvar24h = MAX(relhumidity) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) - MIN(relhumidity) OVER (PARTITION BY TRIM(monitorcode) ORDER BY CAST(readtimestamp AS TIMESTAMP) RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
- Cleaning interval days (cleanintervaldays): Number of days between the last cleaning date and the next cleaning due date. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: cleanintervaldays = JULIANDAY(nextcleaningdue) - JULIANDAY(lastcleaningdate)
- PM2.5/PM10 ratio: Percentage of PM10 particulate matter that is PM2.5
  Definition: pm25conc / pm10conc * 100
- coarse particulate matter (PM10-PM2.5): Difference between PM10 and PM2.5 concentration
  Definition: pm10conc - pm25conc
</domain_knowledge>

<domain_knowledge>
- Cleaning interval days (cleanintervaldays): Number of days between the last cleaning date and the next cleaning due date. Selects 1% of rows.
  Definition: cleanintervaldays = JULIANDAY(nextcleaningdue) - JULIANDAY(lastcleaningdate)
- Conservation difficulty: Level of effort needed to conserve an artifact, inferred from stability and deterioration. Selects 32% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid' THEN 'High' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Medium' END
- High conservation difficulty cohort: Artifacts requiring high conservation effort due to unstable material or rapid deterioration. Selects 17% of rows.
  Definition: conservediff = 'High' AND (matstability = 'Unstable' OR deteriorrate = 'Rapid')
- Stable artifact cohort: Artifacts with stable material, slow deterioration, and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: matstability = 'Stable' AND deteriorrate = 'Slow' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- High public access artifact cohort: Artifacts suitable for high public access based on stability and low conservation difficulty. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: publicaccessrating >= 8 AND matstability = 'Stable' AND conservediff = 'Low'
- Deterioration rate: Rate at which an artifact deteriorates, inferred from material stability. Selects 35% of rows.
  Definition: deteriorrate = CASE WHEN matstability = 'Unstable' THEN 'Rapid' WHEN matstability = 'Stable' THEN 'Slow' ELSE 'Moderate' END

- Click-through rate (CTR): Fraction of page views that result in a click. Selects 5% of rows.
  Definition: ctrval = seshclicks / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- Duration per page view (DPV): Average session duration spent per page view.
  Definition: seshdur / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- Long-session article view: Session lasting longer than the article's estimated reading time.
  Definition: seshdur > readsec
- High-quality article session: Session where a high-quality article was viewed with high engagement.
  Definition: qualscore > 0.8 AND engscore > 0.5
- Recommendation overperformance: Recommendation whose score exceeds the session's click-through rate.
  Definition: recscore > ctrval
- Relevance-utility gap: Difference between session relevance score and recommendation utility score.
  Definition: relscore - recutil
- Bounce session: Session that viewed exactly one page. Selects 3% of rows.
  Definition: seshviews = 1
</domain_knowledge>

SELECT

</definitions>

<task>
Generate a report showing article engagement metrics grouped by category. For each article, calculate both the Article Quality Index (AQI) and Article Readability Score (ARS), then output the article category name with a JSON array containing each article's ID, category, calculated AQI score and ARS score (field names are 'artkey', 'catlabel', 'aqi', and 'ars').
<definitions> MUST USE
- Article Quality Index (AQI): Determines the quality index of an article by integrating quality score, freshness, sentiment, and controversy factors.
  Definition: AQI = ((qualscore + freshscore + sentscore - contrscore)) / (3), where each score is normalized on a uniform scale.
- Article Readability Score (ARS): Calculates the readability of an article by correlating estimated reading time with word count and difficulty factor.
  Definition: ARS = (readsec * log(wordlen)) / (w), where w is a weight factor assigned according to the article difficulty level (e.g., 1 for Basic, 1.5 for Intermediate, 2 for Advanced, 1.2 for others).
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH article_scores AS (
  SELECT
    artkey,
    catlabel,
    (qualscore + freshscore + sentscore - contrscore) / 3.0 AS aqi,
    (readsec * log(wordlen)) / CASE difflevel WHEN 'Basic' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'Intermediate' THEN 1.5 WHEN 'Advanced' THEN 2.0 ELSE 1.2 END AS ars
  FROM articles
)
SELECT
  catlabel,
  json_group_array(
    json_object(
      'artkey', artkey,
      'catlabel', catlabel,
      'aqi', aqi,
      'ars', ars
    )
  ) AS article_metrics
FROM article_scores
GROUP BY catlabel;

For each session, I want to evaluate its Real-Time Session Efficiency (RTSE) by comparing the Content Interaction Efficiency (CIE) against the Session Bounce Rate Adjustment (SBRA). Please show me session ID, start time, SBRA, average sequence value from interactions, and the resulting RTSE. Make sure the results avoid divide-by-zero errors.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Real-Time Session Efficiency (RTSE): Evaluates session efficiency by balancing interaction outcomes against bounce adjustments.
  Definition: RTSE = (CIE) / (SBRA), where CIE denotes the Content Interaction Efficiency and SBRA is the Session Bounce Rate Adjustment.
- Session Bounce Rate Adjustment (SBRA): Adjusts the raw session bounce rate by factoring in the click-through rate to better understand session quality.
  Definition: SBRA = bncrate * (1 - (ctrval) / (100)), where bncrate is the bounce rate and ctrval is the click-through rate percentage.
- Content Interaction Efficiency (CIE): Measures how efficiently a user interacts with content inside a session by looking at the average relative order in which events occur (their sequence values)
  Definition: CIE = AVG(seqval)

Here `seqval` is the event’s sequence/position within a session (e.g., 1, 2, 3…).  Average it across all interactions in a session.
</definitions>

candidates:
WITH session_bounce AS
  (SELECT s.seshkey,
          s.seshstart,
          s.bncrate * (1 - s.ctrval / 100.0) AS sbra
   FROM sessions s),
     session_interaction_avg AS
  (SELECT i.seshlink2,
          AVG(i.seqval) AS avg_sequence_value
   FROM interactions i
   GROUP BY i.seshlink2)
SELECT sb.seshkey,
       sb.seshstart,
       sb.sbra,
       sia.avg_sequence_value,
       CAST(sia.avg_sequence_value AS REAL) / NULLIF(sb.sbra, 0) AS rtse
FROM session_bounce sb
LEFT JOIN session_interaction_avg sia ON sb.seshkey = sia.seshlink2;

<domain_knowledge>
- click metadata: Click events include click type, click source, and click context. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clktype), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clksrc), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clkctx), '') <> ''
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- click position (clkpos): Ordinal position of a click event among click events by click timestamp.
  Definition: clkpos = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY evttype ORDER BY clkts)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- interaction identifier (intkey): Unique integer identifier for each interaction row, ordered by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: intkey = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY intts DESC)
- click event: An interaction whose event type is click and that has a click timestamp. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND clkts IS NOT NULL
- homepage click: A click event whose click source is the homepage. Selects 6% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND TRIM(clksrc) = 'Homepage'

<definitions> MUST USE
- Real-Time Session Efficiency (RTSE): Evaluates session efficiency by balancing interaction outcomes against bounce adjustments.
  Definition: RTSE = (CIE) / (SBRA), where CIE denotes the Content Interaction Efficiency and SBRA is the Session Bounce Rate Adjustment.
- Session Bounce Rate Adjustment (SBRA): Adjusts the raw session bounce rate by factoring in the click-through rate to better understand session quality.
  Definition: SBRA = bncrate * (1 - (ctrval) / (100)), where bncrate is the bounce rate and ctrval is the click-through rate percentage.
- Content Interaction Efficiency (CIE): Measures how efficiently a user interacts with content inside a session by looking at the average relative order in which events occur (their sequence values)
  Definition: CIE = AVG(seqval)

Here `seqval` is the event’s sequence/position within a session (e.g., 1, 2, 3…).  Average it across all interactions in a session.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH session_bounce AS (
    SELECT s.seshkey,
           s.seshstart,
           s.bncrate * (1 - s.ctrval / 100.0) AS sbra
    FROM sessions s
),
session_interaction_avg AS (
    SELECT i.seshlink2,
           AVG(i.seqval) AS avg_sequence_value
    FROM interactions i
    GROUP BY i.seshlink2
)
SELECT sb.seshkey,
       sb.seshstart,
       sb.sbra,
       sia.avg_sequence_value,
       CAST(sia.avg_sequence_value AS REAL) / NULLIF(sb.sbra, 0) AS rtse
FROM session_bounce sb
LEFT JOIN session_interaction_avg sia ON sb.seshkey = sia.seshlink2;

- User Demographic Score (UDS): Measures the impact of user demographics by combining age with factors related to gender and occupation.
  Definition: UDS = ageval * genderFactor * occupationFactor, where genderFactor and occupationFactor are weights derived from segmentation studies.

  Definition: 'Premium' = 2.0, 'Enterprise' = 3.0, 'Basic' = 1.0, and others = 0.5. It reflects the assumed revenue or importance of the subscription tier.

<task>
For each combination of subscription status, gender, occupation, and age group, I want to examine how users differ in terms of their User Subscription Value (USV) and User Demographic Score (UDS). Only include segments with more than 10 users, and show me the group's subscription type, gender, occupation, age group bucket ('Under 25', '25-34', '35-44', '45-54', '55+'), number of users, average USV, average UDS, average satisfaction score, and the shared interests as a comma-separated list. Return the top 15 groups ranked by average USV (descending), and break ties using average UDS.
<definitions> MUST USE
- User Subscription Value (USV): Evaluates the relative value of a user's subscription based on subscription duration and status.
  Definition: USV = subdays * statusWeight, where statusWeight is a multiplier defined by the subscription status (for example, Premium, Enterprise, or Basic).
- User Demographic Score (UDS): Measures the impact of user demographics by combining age with factors related to gender and occupation.
  Definition: UDS = ageval * genderFactor * occupationFactor, where genderFactor and occupationFactor are weights derived from segmentation studies.
- genderFactor: A weighting value used to balance gender representation in demographic scoring.
  Definition: Assigned as 1.0 for Male, Female, and 0.8 otherwise. It standardizes the gender effect on demographic impact.
- occupationFactor: A multiplier that reflects how user occupation contributes to their demographic value.
  Definition: 'Professional' = 1.5, 'Retired' = 1.2, 'Student' = 0.7, 'Other' = 1.0. These values are based on segmentation assumptions or business rules.
- statusWeight: A weight assigned to different subscription tiers to reflect their business value.
  Definition: 'Premium' = 2.0, 'Enterprise' = 3.0, 'Basic' = 1.0, and others = 0.5. It reflects the assumed revenue or importance of the subscription tier.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE
base AS (
  SELECT
    u.userkey,
    u.substatus,
    u.gendlbl,
    u.occulbl,
    CASE
      WHEN u.ageval < 25 THEN 'Under 25'
      WHEN u.ageval <= 34 THEN '25-34'
      WHEN u.ageval <= 44 THEN '35-44'
      WHEN u.ageval <= 54 THEN '45-54'
      ELSE '55+'
    END AS age_group,
    u.subdays * CASE TRIM(u.substatus)
      WHEN 'Premium' THEN 2.0
      WHEN 'Enterprise' THEN 3.0
      WHEN 'Basic' THEN 1.0
      ELSE 0.5
    END AS usv,
    u.ageval * CASE WHEN TRIM(u.gendlbl) IN ('F', 'M') THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.8 END
      * CASE TRIM(u.occulbl)
          WHEN 'Professional' THEN 1.5
          WHEN 'Retired' THEN 1.2
          WHEN 'Student' THEN 0.7
          ELSE 1.0
        END AS uds,
    CAST(json_extract(u.user_preferences, '$.satisfaction_score') AS REAL) AS satisfaction_score,
    COALESCE(json_extract(u.user_preferences, '$.interests'), '') AS interests
  FROM users u
),
groups AS (
  SELECT
    substatus,
    gendlbl,
    occulbl,
    age_group,
    COUNT(*) AS num_users,
    AVG(usv) AS avg_usv,
    AVG(uds) AS avg_uds,
    AVG(satisfaction_score) AS avg_satisfaction_score
  FROM base
  GROUP BY substatus, gendlbl, occulbl, age_group
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
),
split_interests AS (
  SELECT
    userkey,
    substatus,
    gendlbl,
    occulbl,
    age_group,
    TRIM(SUBSTR(interests, 1, INSTR(interests || ',', ',') - 1)) AS interest,
    SUBSTR(interests || ',', INSTR(interests || ',', ',') + 1) AS rest
  FROM base
  WHERE TRIM(interests) <> ''
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    userkey,
    substatus,
    gendlbl,
    occulbl,
    age_group,
    TRIM(SUBSTR(rest, 1, INSTR(rest, ',') - 1)) AS interest,
    SUBSTR(rest, INSTR(rest, ',') + 1) AS rest
  FROM split_interests
  WHERE rest <> ''
),
interests_agg AS (
  SELECT
    substatus,
    gendlbl,
    occulbl,
    age_group,
    GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT interest) AS shared_interests
  FROM split_interests
  WHERE interest <> ''
  GROUP BY substatus, gendlbl, occulbl, age_group
)
SELECT
  g.substatus,
  g.gendlbl,
  g.occulbl,
  g.age_group,
  g.num_users,
  g.avg_usv,
  g.avg_uds,
  g.avg_satisfaction_score,
  COALESCE(i.shared_interests, '') AS shared_interests
FROM groups g
LEFT JOIN interests_agg i
  ON g.substatus = i.substatus
 AND g.gendlbl = i.gendlbl
 AND g.occulbl = i.occulbl
 AND g.age_group = i.age_group
ORDER BY g.avg_usv DESC, g.avg_uds DESC
LIMIT 15;
```

I want to monitor System Performance Index (SPI) and detect potential slowdowns. For every system performance record with response time over 100 ms, show me the trace ID, actual response time, load score, performance score, a computed performance delta (difference between perfscore and loadscore), the rank of that response time among all alerts (high to low), and a performance status label ('Critical', 'Warning', or 'Normal') based on Performance Status.
<definitions> MUST USE
- System Performance Index (SPI): Measures overall system performance by considering response time, load, and performance scores.
  Definition: SPI = ((perfscore - loadscore) * 100) / (resptime), where resptime is measured in milliseconds.
- Performance Status: Categorizes system records based on response time into Critical, Warning, or Normal bands.
  Definition: A CASE-based classification where resptime > 200 is 'Critical', >150 is 'Warning', and others are 'Normal'.
</definitions>

       sp.resptime,
       sp.loadscore,
       sp.perfscore,
       sp.perfscore - sp.loadscore AS performance_delta,

       CASE
           WHEN sp.resptime > 200 THEN 'Critical'
           WHEN sp.resptime > 150 THEN 'Warning'
           ELSE 'Normal'
       END AS performance_status
FROM systemperformance AS sp
WHERE sp.resptime > 100
ORDER BY resptime_rank;

- interaction identifier (intkey): Unique integer identifier for each interaction row, ordered by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: intkey = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY intts DESC)
- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- High-quality article session: Session where a high-quality article was viewed with high engagement.
  Definition: qualscore > 0.8 AND engscore > 0.5
- Relevance-utility gap: Difference between session relevance score and recommendation utility score.
  Definition: relscore - recutil
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- Hybrid recommendation: A recommendation generated using the Hybrid algorithm label. Selects 27% of rows.
  Definition: alglabel = 'Hybrid'
- Trending recommendation: A recommendation with the Trending strategy label. Selects 25% of rows.
  Definition: stratlabel = 'Trending'
- Personalized recommendation: A recommendation with the Personalized strategy label. Selects 23% of rows.
  Definition: stratlabel = 'Personalized'

I want to monitor System Performance Index (SPI) and detect potential slowdowns. For every system performance record with response time over 100 ms, show me the trace ID, actual response time, load score, performance score, a computed performance delta (difference between perfscore and loadscore), the rank of that response time among all alerts (high to low), and a performance status label ('Critical', 'Warning', or 'Normal') based on Performance Status.
<definitions> MUST USE
- System Performance Index (SPI): Measures overall system performance by considering response time, load, and performance scores.
  Definition: SPI = ((perfscore - loadscore) * 100) / (resptime), where resptime is measured in milliseconds.
- Performance Status: Categorizes system records based on response time into Critical, Warning, or Normal bands.
  Definition: A CASE-based classification where resptime > 200 is 'Critical', >150 is 'Warning', and others are 'Normal'.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

SELECT sp.rectrace, sp.resptime, sp.loadscore, sp.perfscore,
       sp.perfscore - sp.loadscore AS performance_delta,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sp.resptime DESC) AS resptime_rank,
       CASE WHEN sp.resptime > 200 THEN 'Critical'
            WHEN sp.resptime > 150 THEN 'Warning'
            ELSE 'Normal'
       END AS performance_status
FROM systemperformance AS sp
WHERE sp.resptime > 100
ORDER BY resptime_rank;

<domain_knowledge>
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- Duration per page view (DPV): Average session duration spent per page view.
  Definition: seshdur / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- click metadata: Click events include click type, click source, and click context. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clktype), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clksrc), '') <> '' AND COALESCE(TRIM(clkctx), '') <> ''
- High-quality article session: Session where a high-quality article was viewed with high engagement.
  Definition: qualscore > 0.8 AND engscore > 0.5
- Recommendation overperformance: Recommendation whose score exceeds the session's click-through rate.
  Definition: recscore > ctrval
- Relevance-utility gap: Difference between session relevance score and recommendation utility score.
  Definition: relscore - recutil
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
I need to analyze sessions using the Session Bounce Rate Adjustment (SBRA) concept to understand relationships between bounce rates and click-through rates. For each combination of user type, user segment, and performance segment category, show them with the count of sessions, average raw bounce rates, average adjusted bounce rates, CTR, engagement score, duration, and page views. Only include segments with more than 10 sessions and order by adjusted bounce rate and CTR.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Session Bounce Rate Adjustment (SBRA): Adjusts the raw session bounce rate by factoring in the click-through rate to better understand session quality.
  Definition: SBRA = bncrate * (1 - (ctrval) / (100)), where bncrate is the bounce rate and ctrval is the click-through rate percentage.
- Bounce Percentile: Ranks sessions by their adjusted bounce rate relative to all other sessions.
  Definition: A percentile ranking computed using PERCENT_RANK() over all sessions ordered by adjusted_bounce_rate.
- CTR Percentile: Ranks sessions by their click-through rate relative to all other sessions.
  Definition: A percentile ranking computed using PERCENT_RANK() over all sessions ordered by ctrval in descending order.
- Performance Segment: Categorizes sessions based on their relative bounce rate and CTR performance using percentile rankings.
  Definition: A classification of sessions into performance categories based on specific percentile criteria: 'High Bounce, Low CTR' (bounce_percentile < 0.25, ctr_percentile < 0.25), 'High Bounce, High CTR' (bounce_percentile < 0.25, ctr_percentile >= 0.75), 'Low Bounce, Low CTR' (bounce_percentile >= 0.75, ctr_percentile < 0.25), 'Low Bounce, High CTR' (bounce_percentile >= 0.75, ctr_percentile >= 0.75), or 'Average Performance' for all other combinations.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        s.bncrate,
        s.ctrval,
        s.engscore,
        s.seshdur,
        s.seshviews,
        u.typelabel,
        u.seglabel,
        s.bncrate * (1 - s.ctrval / 100.0) AS adjusted_bounce_rate
    FROM sessions AS s
    JOIN users AS u ON s.userel = u.userkey
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        bncrate,
        ctrval,
        engscore,
        seshdur,
        seshviews,
        typelabel,
        seglabel,
        adjusted_bounce_rate,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY adjusted_bounce_rate DESC) AS bounce_percentile,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ctrval) AS ctr_percentile
    FROM base
),
classified AS (
    SELECT
        bncrate,
        ctrval,
        engscore,
        seshdur,
        seshviews,
        typelabel,
        seglabel,
        adjusted_bounce_rate,
        bounce_percentile,
        ctr_percentile,
        CASE
            WHEN bounce_percentile < 0.25 AND ctr_percentile < 0.25 THEN 'High Bounce, Low CTR'
            WHEN bounce_percentile < 0.25 AND ctr_percentile >= 0.75 THEN 'High Bounce, High CTR'
            WHEN bounce_percentile >= 0.75 AND ctr_percentile < 0.25 THEN 'Low Bounce, Low CTR'
            WHEN bounce_percentile >= 0.75 AND ctr_percentile >= 0.75 THEN 'Low Bounce, High CTR'
            ELSE 'Average Performance'
        END AS performance_segment_category
    FROM ranked
)
SELECT
    typelabel AS user_type,
    seglabel AS user_segment,
    performance_segment_category,
    COUNT(*) AS session_count,
    AVG(bncrate) AS avg_raw_bounce_rate,
    AVG(adjusted_bounce_rate) AS avg_adjusted_bounce_rate,
    AVG(ctrval) AS ctr,
    AVG(engscore) AS engagement_score,
    AVG(seshdur) AS duration,
    AVG(seshviews) AS page_views
FROM classified
GROUP BY typelabel, seglabel, performance_segment_category
HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
ORDER BY avg_adjusted_bounce_rate, ctr;

- interaction identifier (intkey): Unique integer identifier for each interaction row, ordered by interaction timestamp.

- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- click position (clkpos): Ordinal position of a click event among click events by click timestamp.
  Definition: clkpos = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY evttype ORDER BY clkts)
- click event: An interaction whose event type is click and that has a click timestamp. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND clkts IS NOT NULL
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)

  Definition: (Group registrations / Total monthly registrations) * 100
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', regmoment) AS registration_month,
       testgrp,
       COUNT(*) AS total_registrations,
       (100.0 * COUNT(*) / NULLIF(SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY strftime('%Y-%m', regmoment)), 0)) AS cohort_percentage
FROM users
GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', regmoment), testgrp
ORDER BY registration_month, testgrp;

I want to see how Article Readability Score (ARS) impacts Engagement Rate across categories. Show the article category, average readability score, average engagement rate, correlation coefficient per category and count the number of articles within low, medium, and high readability groups based on Readability Segmentation.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Article Readability Score (ARS): Calculates the readability of an article by correlating estimated reading time with word count and difficulty factor.
  Definition: ARS = (readsec * log(wordlen)) / (w), where w is a weight factor assigned according to the article difficulty level (e.g., 1 for Basic, 1.5 for Intermediate, 2 for Advanced, 1.2 for others).
- Readability Weight Mapping: Defines difficulty-based weighting for readability calculations.
  Definition: Difficulty levels are assigned weights: Basic = 1, Intermediate = 1.5, Advanced = 2, Others = 1.2.
- Readability Segmentation: Classifies articles into readability categories based on calculated readability scores.
  Definition: Low readability: ARS < 50, Medium readability: 50 <= ARS <= 100, High readability: ARS > 100.
</definitions>

           END) AS medium_readability_count,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN ars > 100 THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END) AS high_readability_count
FROM article_readability
GROUP BY catlabel;

  Definition: ctrval = seshclicks / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.

<task>
I want to see how Article Readability Score (ARS) impacts Engagement Rate across categories. Show the article category, average readability score, average engagement rate, correlation coefficient per category and count the number of articles within low, medium, and high readability groups based on Readability Segmentation.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Article Readability Score (ARS): Calculates the readability of an article by correlating estimated reading time with word count and difficulty factor.
  Definition: ARS = (readsec * log(wordlen)) / (w), where w is a weight factor assigned according to the article difficulty level (e.g., 1 for Basic, 1.5 for Intermediate, 2 for Advanced, 1.2 for others).
- Readability Weight Mapping: Defines difficulty-based weighting for readability calculations.
  Definition: Difficulty levels are assigned weights: Basic = 1, Intermediate = 1.5, Advanced = 2, Others = 1.2.
- Readability Segmentation: Classifies articles into readability categories based on calculated readability scores.
  Definition: Low readability: ARS < 50, Medium readability: 50 <= ARS <= 100, High readability: ARS > 100.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

WITH article_readability AS (
  SELECT
    a.catlabel,
    (a.readsec * ln(a.wordlen)) /
      CASE a.difflevel
        WHEN 'Basic' THEN 1.0
        WHEN 'Intermediate' THEN 1.5
        WHEN 'Advanced' THEN 2.0
        ELSE 1.2
      END AS ars,
    CAST(json_extract(a.engagement_metrics, '$.engagement_rate') AS REAL) AS engagement_rate
  FROM articles a
)
SELECT
  catlabel,
  AVG(ars) AS avg_readability_score,
  AVG(engagement_rate) AS avg_engagement_rate,
  (CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) * SUM(ars * engagement_rate) - SUM(ars) * SUM(engagement_rate)) /
    NULLIF(
      SQRT(
        (CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) * SUM(ars * ars) - SUM(ars) * SUM(ars)) *
        (CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) * SUM(engagement_rate * engagement_rate) - SUM(engagement_rate) * SUM(engagement_rate))
      ), 0
    ) AS correlation_coefficient,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ars < 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS low_readability_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ars >= 50 AND ars <= 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS medium_readability_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ars > 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_readability_count
FROM article_readability
GROUP BY catlabel;

<domain_knowledge>
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- click position (clkpos): Ordinal position of a click event among click events by click timestamp.
  Definition: clkpos = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY evttype ORDER BY clkts)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- interaction identifier (intkey): Unique integer identifier for each interaction row, ordered by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: intkey = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY intts DESC)
- numeric sequence value (seqval): Numeric sequence of an interaction within its session by interaction timestamp.
  Definition: seqval = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seshlink2 ORDER BY intts)
- click event: An interaction whose event type is click and that has a click timestamp. Selects 22% of rows.
  Definition: TRIM(evttype) = 'click' AND clkts IS NOT NULL
- Recommendation overperformance: Recommendation whose score exceeds the session's click-through rate.
  Definition: recscore > ctrval
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
</domain_knowledge>

<task>
I want to understand how the recommendation position influences user clicks. Could you return the position, total recommendations, total clicks, and recommendation click-through rate (RCTR) for each position. Sort the results by position in ascending order.
<definitions> MUST USE
- Recommendation Position Illustration: Depicts the effect of recommendation placement on user visibility and engagement.
  Definition: A recommendation placed in position 3, for example, may benefit from higher prominence compared to lower-ranked placements.
- Recommendation Click-Through Rate (RCTR): Defines RCTR as the ratio of clicks to total recommendations.
  Definition: RCTR = (clicks / recommendations) when recommendations are greater than zero.
</definitions>
</task>

Return only the SQL, no comments

SELECT r.posval AS position,
       COUNT(DISTINCT r.reckey) AS total_recommendations,
       COUNT(i.intkey) AS total_clicks,
       CAST(COUNT(i.intkey) AS REAL) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT r.reckey), 0) AS rctr
FROM recommendations r
LEFT JOIN interactions i
  ON i.reclink = r.reckey
 AND TRIM(i.evttype) = 'click'
 AND i.clkts IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY r.posval
ORDER BY r.posval;

<domain_knowledge>
- Click-through rate (CTR): Fraction of page views that result in a click. Selects 5% of rows.
  Definition: ctrval = seshclicks / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Clicks per recommendation (CPR): Number of clicks divided by number of recommendations shown.
  Definition: seshclicks / NULLIF(seshrecs, 0)
- Duration per page view (DPV): Average session duration spent per page view.
  Definition: seshdur / NULLIF(seshviews, 0)
- Views per click (VPC): Number of page views per click.
  Definition: seshviews / NULLIF(seshclicks, 0)
- Recommendation-heavy session: Session with more than ten recommendations shown. Selects 85% of rows.
  Definition: seshrecs > 10
- Reading-to-duration ratio: Reading time spent in an interaction divided by total session duration.
  Definition: json_extract(interaction_behavior, '$.time_spent.reading_seconds') / seshdur
- Attention-to-duration ratio: Attention time spent in an interaction divided by total session duration.
  Definition: json_extract(interaction_behavior, '$.time_spent.attention_time') / seshdur
- Long-session article view: Session lasting longer than the article's estimated reading time.
  Definition: seshdur > readsec
- High-quality article session: Session where a high-quality article was viewed with high engagement.
  Definition: qualscore > 0.8 AND engscore > 0.5
- Recommendation overperformance: Recommendation whose score exceeds the session's click-through rate.
  Definition: recscore > ctrval
</domain_knowledge>
